answer: An agent market requires a $100 bond locked for 90 days before an identity can bid. Each bonded identity becomes a vertex in the trading graph; its escrow is a costly signal, not a name check. Creating 10,000 sybils therefore freezes $1 million for a quarter, imposing financing and opportunity costs. Withdrawals move at a glacier pace, preventing an attacker from recycling one bond through a rapid swarm.
